scenes.heading: QuickStart Jar Naming Convention (Part 1 of 2)
scenes.narration: Env Setup. QuickStart Jar Naming Convention (Part 1 of 2). In this video we review 5 key concepts you need to know for the certification.

scenes.question: What is the format of the QuickStart Jar filename?
scenes.heading: aem-<tier>_<environment>-p<port>.jar
scenes.body: The QuickStart Jar filename follows the format `aem-<tier>_<environment>-p<port>.jar`. The tier (author/publish) and optional environment segment control how AEM starts up. The port after `-p` determines the listening port.

scenes.question: What does the filename aem-author-p4502.jar tell AEM when it starts?
scenes.heading: Start as an Author instance in Dev mode on port 4502
scenes.body: `aem-author-p4502.jar` tells AEM to start as an Author instance in the default Dev mode, listening on port 4502. No environment segment means the default dev run mode is used.

scenes.question: What does the filename aem-author_prod-p4502.jar tell AEM when it starts?
scenes.heading: Start as Author in Production mode on port 4502
scenes.body: `aem-author_prod-p4502.jar` starts AEM as an Author instance in Production mode on port 4502. The `_prod` segment sets the environment run mode, which activates production-specific OSGi configurations.

scenes.question: Which part of the QuickStart Jar filename controls the AEM tier?
scenes.heading: The segment after aem- and before the port (author or publish)
scenes.body: In the filename `aem-<tier>_<environment>-p<port>.jar`, the tier is the segment immediately after `aem-`. It must be either `author` or `publish`, and it is locked on first startup.
